 Cold Storage Removes Homegrown Apple Juice Batch After Excessive Mould Toxin Found In Hong Kong
 By George Yang - 2026-11-21 , 11:20 am 
 Cold Storage has removed a batch of Homegrown apple juice from sale after Hong Kong authorities found excessive levels of patulin, a toxin produced by moulds.
 The affected product is Homegrown 100% Pure NZ Apple Juice from New Zealand, sold in one-litre bottles with a best-before date of 11 February 2027 .
 Sample Exceeded Hong Kong’s Legal Limit
 Hong Kong’s Centre for Food Safety issued an alert on 17 November 2026 after testing a sample collected at a wholesale market in Sai Ying Pun under its routine food surveillance programme.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 The sample contained 79 micrograms of patulin per kilogram, exceeding Hong Kong’s legal limit of 50 micrograms per kilogram.
 The centre said the Hong Kong importer had stopped selling the affected batch, removed it from shelves and begun a recall following its instructions.
 Affected Batch Removed From Sale In Singapore
 In a response to 8world published on 21 November, the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) said it had contacted Cold Storage, the local importer. The company then voluntarily withdrew the affected batch.
 SFA also directed the importer to ensure the affected products would not be sold in Singapore and said it would continue monitoring the situation.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Buyers Advised Not To Drink Affected Juice
 SFA explained that patulin is mainly found in rotting apples and apple products. It can withstand heat and may remain after processing. Excessive intake can cause nausea, stomach and intestinal discomfort, and vomiting.
 As a precaution, SFA advised anyone who bought the affected product not to drink it.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Those who have already consumed it and are concerned about their health should seek medical advice. Buyers can contact the shop where they purchased it with enquiries.
